along with thousands more in workforce and career development programs. ACE also supports over 225 hourly instructors, works with 127 plus business partners, and plays a direct role in strengthening the skilled workforce pipeline in Fairfax County.

From a financial standpoint, ACE is already producing significant operating support. ACE generated approximately $3.15 million in tuition income last year and $3.4 million in grant income, totaling over $6 million in combined revenue.

In FY26, ACE demonstrated clear operational improvements by transitioning to a modern registration system, bringing marketing in-house to save $180,000 and generating $70,000 in one weekend through targeted outreach.

Despite these efficiencies, ACE is forecasting a deficit of approximately $600,000. That deficit is not a sign that ACE is failing. It's a sign that the program is productive and essential and operating beyond what its current structure can sustain without your support.

If ACE funding is reduced, Fairfax will lose a proven system that supports adult learners, workforce readiness and adult mobility. I urge the board to prioritize ACE funding because it is efficient, high impact, financially strategic and supports economic mobility.
